paper.title: MD-HIT: Machine learning for material property prediction with dataset redundancy control
paper.research_summary: This paper addresses the overestimation of machine learning model performance in materials science caused by dataset redundancy—i.e., highly similar materials in databases like Materials Project due to historical 'tinkering' in material design. It proposes MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm inspired by bioinformatics’ CD-HIT, with two variants: MD-HIT-composition (using composition-based distances like Mendeleev and MatScholar) and MD-HIT-structure (using structure-based distances like XRD and OFM). The authors apply MD-HIT to generate non-redundant datasets for formation energy and band gap prediction, then evaluate how redundancy control affects the predictive performance (R², MAE) of state-of-the-art ML models (Roost, CrabNet, ALIGNN, DeeperGATGNN), demonstrating that reduced redundancy leads to lower—but more realistic—performance, especially for out-of-distribution (OOD) samples.

tasks.task_name_raw: dataset redundancy control for material property prediction
tasks.objective: Reduce dataset redundancy in materials datasets to enable objective, realistic evaluation of ML model performance—particularly extrapolative (out-of-distribution) capability—by preventing information leakage between training and test sets caused by high similarity among samples.
constraints: must preserve coverage of composition/structure space
must avoid data bias (e.g., over-selection of near-zero band gap samples)
thresholds must be tunable per distance metric
input_requirements: composition descriptors (e.g., MatScholar, Mendeleev features) or structure descriptors (e.g., XRD, OFM features)
output_goal: non-redundant dataset where no pair of samples exceeds a user-defined similarity threshold

evidence.text: In this paper, we survey the overestimated ML performance in materials science for material property prediction and propose MD-HIT, a redundancy reduction algorithm for material datasets.
We propose and develop two material dataset redundancy-reducing algorithms based on a greedy algorithm inspired by the peer bioinformatics CD-HIT algorithm.

stages.stage_goal: Generate non-redundant composition datasets by iteratively selecting representative materials based on composition similarity thresholds.

evidence.text: Our MD-HIT-composition and MD-HIT-structure redundancy reduction algorithms are designed based on this idea, utilizing greedy incremental algorithms. In our case, MD-HIT starts the selection process with a seed material (default to H2O) and then sorts the remaining materials by the number of atoms instead of the formula lengths. Subsequently, it classifies each material as redundant or representative, depending on its similarity to the existing representatives already selected into the cluster.

stages.stage_goal: Generate non-redundant structure datasets by iteratively selecting representative crystal structures based on structure similarity thresholds.

evidence.text: MD-HIT-structure algorithm uses the same greedy adding approach as the MD-HIT-composition, except that it uses a structure-based distance metric.

MD-HIT-structure algorithm also starts the selection process with a seed material (default to H2O) which is put in the non-redundant set. It then sorts the remaining materials in the candidate set by the number of atoms instead of the formula lengths, and classifies them one-by-one as redundant or representative materials based on their similarities (we use Euclidean distance of XRD features or OFM features) to the existing representatives already selected into the non-redundant set.

stages.stage_goal: Acquire and preprocess large-scale materials data from public databases to serve as input for redundancy reduction.

evidence.text: We downloaded 125,619 cif files with material structures from the Materials Project database, which includes 89,354 materials with unique compositions. In cases where compositions corresponded to multiple polymorphs, we adopted average material property values by default, with the exception of formation energy property, for which we used the minimum value. Additionally, we excluded mp-101974 (HeSiO2) due to issues with calculating Matscholar features. After eliminating formulas with over 50 atoms, we obtained a non-duplicate composition dataset with 86,741 samples...

evidence.text: To investigate the impact of redundancy control on structure-based material datasets, we utilized the Materials Project database of 123,108 crystal structures with their formation energy per atom and band gaps.
For Mendeleev similarity, we used distance thresholds of 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, and 3 to generate seven non-redundant datasets (Mendeleev-nr). The dataset sizes range from 86,740 to 3177.
Similarly, we generated eight Matscholar non-redundant datasets (Matscholar-nr) with percentages of the total range from 50.82% to 2.33%.
We also applied the MD-HIT-structure algorithm to all 125,619 structures and used different thresholds to generate seven XRD non-redundant datasets...
